title: Biography
text: Biography From aviation to signal processing My path began in Tehran with electrical engineering and aviation telecommunications. At Beihang I turned to spacecraft navigation, studying how a single image of star trails can reveal a spacecraft’s angular velocity. Today my doctoral research brings me back to signals, and to the decisions we make from them. Education 2026 – present Information & Communication Engineering School of Electronics and Information Engineering, Beihang University · Communication systems · Signal processing Supervisor · Prof. Yanhong Kou 2024 – 2026 M.Eng. in Aerospace Engineering Beihang University, Hangzhou · Space Technology Applications. Thesis on single-frame optical trail imagery for spacecraft angular velocity estimation. GPA 3.14/4.0. 2020 – 2024 B.Eng. in Electrical Engineering Civil Aviation Technology College, Tehran · Aviation telecommunications. Thesis on satellite internet in aviation. Experience 2025.09 – present Head of Research Assistants & Celestia Team Lead SHE Orbit · Safe reinforcement learning for collision avoidance in low Earth orbit under cybersecurity constraints, and autonomy for space robotics. 2024.02 – 2024.07 ICT engineering trainee Iran Airports and Air Navigation Company, Tehran · Air traffic control communications and AI systems. 2023.06 – 2024.02 Citizen scientist European Space Agency, Cologne · EEG analysis in a neurophysiological study of cosmic electromagnetic radiation. Earlier projects Mahbot1 · NASA Astrobee On NASA Astrobee hardware, I integrated lightweight neural networks with ROS for perception and object localization in microgravity. NASA Impact Visual Analysis System (NIVAS) An interactive asteroid-impact simulator using NASA and USGS data, recognized at the NASA Space Apps Challenge in Tokyo. title: Research
text: Communication systems · Signal processing Current research I study signal processing and the mathematics of reliable, timely alerts in dynamical systems. My path to this work began in aviation telecommunications and spacecraft navigation. Alert A Unified Mathematical Framework for Evaluating Detection Reliability, Alert Timeliness, and Safety in Dynamical Systems In the Alert project, I connect three questions. Can a detector distinguish a change from ordinary variation? How much time is left when it raises an alert? What happens to the physical system if it stays silent? Deep-space navigation · Autonomous vehicles · UAVs · Surgical robots Future directions Designing new AI systems My next goal is to design original AI systems, starting from the mathematical questions raised by detection and timely decisions. Quantum navigation & computing I plan to explore quantum formulations for navigation and investigate how to implement them on quantum computers.

title: Research notes
text: Research notes Signal processing Why alert timing matters Imagine a vehicle that needs two seconds to brake. If it will reach an obstacle in ten seconds, its last opportunity to start braking is at eight seconds. Raising a detector’s threshold can delay its first alert beyond that deadline. Estimating reliability would require many trajectories and a model of how they arise. Current research →

text: Art Persian calligraphy & painting I practise Persian calligraphy and naqqāshi-khatt, a form of painting that takes the written letter as its subject. Historical reference · Nastaʿliq panel by Sayyid Amir ʿAli, mid-17th century. The Met, 1999.356. Iranian Calligraphers Association I am a member of the Iranian Calligraphers Association.
